title: Pointwise randomization Parseval identity
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $f$ be a real-valued function on its outcome space, and fix an outcome $x$. The uniform average over $r\in\{0,1\}^n$ of the square of the randomized orthogonal expansion of $f$ at $x$ equals the sum of the squares of its orthogonal components at $x$; that is, $\mathbb E_r[(R_rf(x))^2]=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]} f_S(x)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: A product of n finite probability spaces
A real-valued function on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $x\in\Omega$. If $R_rf(x)=\sum_S\chi_S(r)f_S(x)$ and $r$ is uniform on the Boolean cube, then $\mathbb E_r(R_rf(x))^2=\sum_Sf_S(x)^2$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $\chi_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{r_i}$ for $r\in\{0,1\}^n$.
